title_he: אִם נֵלֵךְ אַחֲרֵי הַדּוֹד נוֹשְׂאִים אֶת־הַצְּלָב
review: The hymn is the pilgrim's trust: 1:1–2 is John 14:1 with Phil 2:12, 2:1–6 is Matt 16:24 with Ps 84:7 (עֵמֶק הַבָּכָא) and Ps 91:1, 3:1–6 is Ps 23:4 with 1 Sam 3:10, and 4:1–6 is Eph 3:18–19 with Jas 1:17.
Stanza 1 is a two-line summons and stanzas 2–4 have six lines each (2/6/6/6), the print's `669.669 – 46.76`; the payload keeps the couplet as the hymn's motto.

2:3 בְּעֵמֶק הַדְּמָעוֹת — the Arabic فِي وَادِي الدُّمُوع is the valley of tears; the Hebrew uses the psalm's עֵמֶק הַבָּכָא (Ps 84:7) and renders it plainly as 'the valley of weeping', because the stanza is walking through it and the psalm's place-name would obscure the image.
4:3 בְּהַכְנָעָה — the Arabic بِالْخُضُوع recurs in stanzas 1, 2 and 4; the Hebrew keeps the same noun each time (הַכְנָעָה), so the hymn's single condition is audible as one word.
